Author: Krishan Pahal
Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 83
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 32868 of 2020
Applicant :- Ajay
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar Srivastava,Mohd. Jamshed Khan,Rajesh Kumar Vishwakar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Girish Tiwari
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.

2. Heard Sri Ajay Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri R.M. Yadav,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
Learned counsel for the first informant is not present.

3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 0112 of 2019, U/S 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act,
Police Station Hayat Nagar, District Sambhal, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant, who happens to be the husband of the deceased person, is stated to have subjected her to cruelty for a demand of dowry, as such, he is stated to have strangulated her to death on 1.4.2019.

1 5.

Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence.
The statement of P.W. 1- first informant has been recorded.
Learned counsel has next stated that that as per the statement of the informant P.W. 1, he has categorically stated that the applicant had informed him of the death of the deceased person by hanging.
Learned counsel has stated that there is no likelihood of the conclusion of trial in the near future.
6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further stated that there is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 14.4.2019.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the said allegation itself stands falsified from the fact that the death of the deceased has been caused by strangulation and not by hanging, which negates the said story, whereby the statement of P.W. 1 is intact and he has categorically reiterated the allegations levelled in the FIR.

The applicant being the husband, is the main accused person, as his wife has expired within the precincts of his house and the prosecution has successfully proved the other ingredients of Section 304-B IPC.
8.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, nature of offence, evidence on record, pending trial and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
9. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

10. However, it is directed that the court below may proceed with the trial and reach at the logical conclusion expeditiously, if there is no legal impediment, within a period of one year from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.

11. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 19.1.2023
